A: Axial brain CT panel from a patient with Fahr syndrome shows bilateral putamen calcifications, a classic manifestation of primary familial brain calcification. Arrows annotate the calcifications. B: Axial brain CT panel shows calcifications in the posterior limb of the internal capsule, consistent with white matter calcification in primary familial brain calcification; this location is a recognized but less common pattern than basal ganglia calcification. C: Axial brain CT panel demonstrates bilateral asymmetrical punctate and linear white matter calcifications in the corona radiata, compatible with primary familial brain calcification. The asymmetrical white matter pattern is a recognized less common form. D: Sagittal brain CT panel shows punctate and linear calcifications in the left corona radiata, consistent with white matter calcification in primary familial brain calcification. This is a recognized less common imaging pattern.
